BBC, 24 Nov

Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

Andy Burnham says he is \"not persuaded\" by the case for more powers

The first minister says he wants an urgent meeting with the prime minister after Andy Burnham rejected calls to give more powers to the Welsh government.

Rhun ap Iorwerth said he was \"deeply disappointed\" and that Burnham \"does not view Wales as an equal nation\".

Meanwhile, Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates urged Burnham to \"negotiate around a table\" with ap Iorwerth.

In a letter to ap Iorwerth last week, the prime minister said he was \"not persuaded\" by the case to devolve policing and justice, the Crown Estate and rail infrastructure to Wales.

Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock said the UK government believed \"devolution must be about more than transferring powers from one government to another\".

Trade union body TUC Cymru said it was disappointing calls for further devolution had been \"dismissed without any discussion\".

In a written statement to Senedd members, the first minister said: \"The refusal to even explore the devolution of the crown estate, justice and policing, and rail infrastructure proves that the prime minister does not view Wales as an equal nation.

\"The case in favour of Wales having control over these areas of responsibility - just like Scotland - is compelling. Several commissions have argued for the devolution of justice and policing, yet the UK government seemingly prefers to put unionist ideology before hard evidence.

\"This government is not interested in more powers for power's sake. The current settlement is unfair, unjust and unsustainable.\"

Rhun ap Iorwerth is Plaid Cymru leader and first minister of Wales

In a letter to the prime minister, ap Iorwerth asked the prime minister to reconsider the work of previous reports on the issue.

He said he would \"welcome an urgent meeting with you to discuss the evidence and agree a substantive way forward\".

Meanwhile, Skates called on the Welsh and UK governments to continue talks on the devolution of powers.

He called for \"greater detail\" on why further devolution of policing was not happening, and said he will be meeting with Burnham himself.

Welsh Labour has not dropped calls for the devolution of justice, the Crown Estate and rail investment.

\"You negotiate around a table,\" he said. \"And you don't walk away when work needs to continue. Devolution is a process, not an event and Welsh Labour's position remains clear that we support further devolution to and within Wales.\"

Skates continued: \"Devolution of employment support is vital in getting to grips with the crisis of youth unemployment. The devolution of innovation funding will help strengthen the economy.

\"Devolution of youth justice will lead to better integration of youth services and social services and the justice system.

\"We need action as fast as possible in bringing these powers to Wales and in ensuring they go to the right people and places.

\"On policing, progress is being made, but I want greater detail over why full devolution is not happening as part of the current reforms.\"

Meanwhile, TUC Cymru's general secretary, Laura Doel, said: \"Our focus is on securing the powers and resources needed to improve outcomes for working people. That must include fair funding for Wales.

\"These are the long-established views of TUC Cymru and it's disappointing that our calls have been dismissed without any discussion.

\"We ask that the UK government does more to respect and engage with the democratic institutions in Wales and listens to the voice of Welsh workers, rather than closing down proposals for further devolution before they have been properly considered.\"

Kinnock said: \"The prime minister's offer reflects our view that devolution must be about more than transferring powers from one government to another and that he instead wants each government to consider, alongside local authority partners, how we can empower Welsh regions to use both reserved and devolved powers to drive economic growth.

\"What matters is what works.\"

Neon signs made for Stanley Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut film were among the props that went under the hammer in south-west London last week.

God's Own Junk Yard also had pieces made for Tomb Raider, Bridget Jones's Diary and Elton John for sale on Thursday at its workshop on Lots Road, Fulham.

Matthew Bracey, from the family-run business, says materials used to make traditional neon are becoming harder to find as LEDs take over.

He believes neon could be worth more than gold in 10 years' time.
